bio: Some things never go out of fashion… This quintessential Sologne posthouse with a half-timbered, pink brick façade and stone walls that date back to the 17C, boasts former guests of the likes of none other than Mistinguett and Maurice Chevalier. Take a seat in this timeless setting, depicted by massive oak beams, Gien earthenware and crystal glassware and admire the grounds planted with century-old trees. The enticingly entitled concise menu and tasting menu mingle classical roots with a hint of modernity. While seafood is a firm fixture (splendid tartare of red mullet in a gutsy jus), the chef avows a weakness for red meat and game in particular.
